Denominator is the literal 17; if the class turns out not to have 17 members the number is off (stderr prints the class size). Ambiguity and alt_measured: source (d) uses seed 41,000,000 + i, the same per-request seed as Day-1 #3 sample 0, which the theory's scope says to leave out (it lists only T1, b614, 456c, but e383 has the same seed at T 1.5); alt_measured drops (d). Note the pool mixes T 0.6 (e) and T 1.5 (d) samples with T 1.0 ones, as the recipe says. If a fetch fails, the script reports not_computable rather than silently counting the source as empty.

Same files, pool and rules as k=1. A = solved / |rl_k >= 1 class|, B = solved / |rl_k == 0 class| over base_k == 0 problems of pool_k_le3.json, using the actual class sizes (expected 17 and 16). Refuted if A - B <= 0.0. An empty class gives not_computable (the recipe does not say an empty class refutes). alt_measured: A - B with source (d) (frustea e383, same per-request seed as Day-1 #3 sample 0) left out. Problems 0-99 get one extra sample from (f) and problems 0-2 lack (c), so per-problem sample counts differ between classes; with about 6-10 samples per problem this difference in pool size, not only base rates, can move A - B.

Same 17 problems and sources as k=1. Samples: every Day-1 #3 row with attempt 1 or 2, one entry per vectors.json arm where not None, every e383 attempt-0 row, every F_math500 row, every screen100 per_problem row. Statistic: sum of right / number of samples, pooled over problems (not a mean of per-problem rates). Cap hits count as wrong samples (stored or recomputed score). alt_measured drops source (d) (same per-request seed as Day-1 #3 sample 0, at T 1.5). The Day-1 #3 sample 0-3 attempt-0 rows are not in the pool (the recipe takes only attempts 1 and 2); including them would add 68 wrong samples and lower the rate a lot. Restart rows exist only for problems whose samples hit the cap, so these problems are weighted by their cap-hit count. stderr prints n and right per source.
